subtext.hi: Famous Thales Theorem — geometry ka sabse important theorem!
subtext.en: The famous Thales Theorem — one of the most important theorems in geometry!

text.hi: Agar ek line triangle ki do sides ko proportional parts mein divide karti hai, to woh line third side ke parallel hoti hai — yahi Thales Theorem hai.
text.en: If a line divides two sides of a triangle in proportional parts, that line is parallel to the third side — this is the Thales Theorem.

content.hi: Theorem: ΔABC mein D, AB pe hai aur E, AC pe hai. Agar DE || BC, to AD/DB = AE/EC.
content.en: Theorem: In ΔABC, D is on AB and E is on AC. If DE || BC, then AD/DB = AE/EC.

content.hi: Converse bhi true hai: agar AD/DB = AE/EC, to DE || BC.
content.en: The converse is also true: if AD/DB = AE/EC, then DE || BC.

content.hi: Proof: ΔADE aur ΔABC mein ∠A common hai, ∠ADE=∠ABC aur ∠AED=∠ACB (corresponding angles, DE||BC). Isliye ΔADE~ΔABC (AA), aur AD/AB=AE/AC=DE/BC — isse AD/DB=AE/EC nikalta hai.
content.en: Proof: In ΔADE and ΔABC, ∠A is common, ∠ADE=∠ABC and ∠AED=∠ACB (corresponding angles, DE||BC). So ΔADE~ΔABC (AA), and AD/AB=AE/AC=DE/BC — from which AD/DB=AE/EC follows.

explanation.content: If DE || BC, then AD/DB = AE/EC   |   Converse: If AD/DB = AE/EC, then DE || BC

problem.hi: ΔABC mein DE||BC, D on AB, E on AC. AD=3cm, DB=5cm, AE=4.5cm. EC nikaalo.
problem.en: In ΔABC, DE||BC, D on AB, E on AC. AD=3cm, DB=5cm, AE=4.5cm. Find EC.

problem.hi: DE||BC. AD=x, DB=x−2, AE=x+2, EC=x−1. x nikaalo.
problem.en: DE||BC. AD=x, DB=x−2, AE=x+2, EC=x−1. Find x.

question.en: In ΔABC, DE||BC. AD=2,DB=3,AE=4. Find EC.

explanation.hi: AD/DB=1/2, AE/EC=1/2 — equal, converse se DE||BC.
explanation.en: AD/DB=1/2, AE/EC=1/2 — equal, so by converse DE||BC.

question.hi: Thales Theorem ko Basic Proportionality Theorem bhi kehte hain.
question.en: Thales Theorem is also called Basic Proportionality Theorem.

explanation.hi: Sahi — dono naam same theorem ke hain.
explanation.en: True — both names refer to the same theorem.

summary.hi: Thales Theorem se missing length nikaalo, ya ratios check karke parallel prove karo — dono directions mein kaam aata hai.
summary.en: Use the Thales Theorem to find a missing length, or check ratios to prove parallelism — it works both ways.
